name: LT1357 / LT1358 / LT1359 (single/dual/quad 25 MHz, 600 V/µs C-Load bipolar)
tagline: Lower-power (2 mA/amp) sibling of the LT1364, rated 25 MHz and 600 V/µs. A niche sound-card buffer pick that forum listeners call warm, bright and tonally rich.
technology: Bipolar, built on Linear Technology's complementary bipolar process. It is a single-stage voltage-feedback amplifier with matched high-impedance inputs and the slewing performance of a current-feedback amplifier, and it is stable with any capacitive load (C-Load). Per the ADI/Linear datasheets, the single-stage design settles well. The family comes in 25, 50 and 70 MHz versions at about 2, 4 and 6 mA per amplifier, each as a single, dual and quad. The LT1357 datasheet's front-page typical application is a DAC I-to-V converter.
manufacturers: Analog Devices (acquired Linear Technology in 2017; current vendor)

lineage.notes: Part of the LT1354–LT1365 C-Load family of fast bipolar op amps. The LT1364/LT1365 datasheet (13645fa Rev A) lists the LT1358/LT1359 as the 'Lower Power Version of LT1364/LT1365', with VOS = 0.6 mV and 2 mA per amplifier. Third-party mirrors (alldatasheet, radiolocman) hold Linear-branded copies.

ADI hosts datasheet 135859fb (LT1358/LT1359) and 1357fa (LT1357) at analog.com, and has product pages for the LT1357, LT1358 and LT1359. radiolocman lists separate Linear-branded and ADI-branded LT1358 datasheet entries. No second sources are known.

reputation.summary: A niche pick from the op-amp-rolling era of sound cards (Asus Xonar, Audiotrak Prodigy HD2). Forum posts describe the LT1358 as 'warm, bright, tonal rich and sounds forward'. Some posters prefer it to the faster, higher-current LT1364 in buffer duty, and it is named alongside the LT1364 and LT1361 for buffer positions. The evidence is subjective forum impressions only. No Audio Science Review, Samuel Groner or other measurement data was found for the LT1357/8/9.
typical_uses: Sound-card op-amp swaps (Asus Xonar, Audiotrak Prodigy HD2 buffer/output stage)
Buffer and I/V stages in DIY DACs (the LT1357 datasheet's front-page application is a DAC I-to-V converter)
Wideband amplifiers, buffers, active filters, data acquisition and video/cable drivers (datasheet application list)
caveats: The praise rests on a few subjective forum posts from one discovery lens, and those posts were not re-checked in this pass, so confidence is low.
This is a 25 MHz / 600 V/µs part: keep the layout tight and decouple locally. C-Load stability helps with capacitive loads but not with poor bypassing or long socket leads.

This is a low-power (2.5 mA max per amplifier) part. The datasheet guarantees ±12.5 V into 500 Ω, but output current was not verified, so check it before driving headphones or low impedances directly.
Bipolar inputs: input bias current is up to 500 nA max. Watch for offset with high source impedances.
The supply range is ±2.5 V to ±15 V, so ±15 V is the top of the range and a ±18 V rail is out of spec.

counterfeit_notes: No counterfeit or remark reports specific to the LT1357/LT1358/LT1359 were found. Web search this pass was limited to five queries, so this is not a clean bill of health. Buy from authorized ADI distributors, and treat marketplace 'LT1358' DIP-8s with suspicion, especially leaded (non-#PBF) parts sold as new. A bench check helps: a slow part remarked as an LT1358 cannot reach about 600 V/µs slew or 25 MHz GBW, and supply current should be at most 2.5 mA per amplifier. Also compare the laser marking and date code against known-genuine Linear/ADI parts.

revision_chain_notes: I used all 4 WebSearch calls and no other research tools. For the LT1357 (1357f), the chain is: original 1357f (© 1994, no copy identified) -> Rev A 1357fa, footer 'LT/TP 0598 REV A 2K', May 1998, which is current at analog.com and was confirmed in the search summary. A later revision is not known and probably never existed. Missing: a copy verifiably holding the original 1357f. The alldatasheet id 70419 and 694834, datasheetcatalog, digchip, datasheet4u 51462, Farnell 60377 and datasheet.hk copies are candidates, but none showed its revision footer. For the LT1358/LT1359 (135859f), the chain is: original 135859f (date unknown, probably about 1994) -> Rev A 135859fa (not seen anywhere; searches for '135859fa' returned nothing specific) -> Rev B 135859fb (current at ADI, Mouser and Richardson; date and LT/TP footer not shown). Missing: the dates and footers of all three 135859f revisions, and any copy of the original or Rev A. The Linear-branded mirrors (radiolocman di=339481 and di=80309 (LT1358CN8), alldatasheet 70420, datasheet4u 51465, Scribd 760623506) are the best candidates for pre-Rev-B editions but are unconfirmed. The ADI-branded mirrors (radiolocman di=524267, rlocman.es di=151039) are probably Rev B. No second sources and no acquirer re-issue under a new document number were found. ADI kept the LTC file codes. Unverified lead: docs.rs-online.com/f061/0900766b81222afc.pdf came up twice for LT1358/LT1359 revision queries, but its title and content were not shown, so it was not recorded. The archive_seed_urls follow the standard legacy Linear Technology URL patterns (cds.linear.com/docs/en/datasheet/<code>.pdf, www.linear.com/docs/Datasheet/<code>.pdf, www.linear.com/product/<part>) applied to the verified file codes. They are pattern-derived for Wayback lookup and were not seen in search results.
